title: Observed biodiversity — iNaturalist (Ecuador)
description: ArcGIS Living Atlas' live iNaturalist feed, over Ecuador and the Galápagos: pre-aggregated H3 cells for full coverage and a sample of recent observations as dots. No download and no ETL.

list.name: resolucion
list.label: Resolution
list.description: El id de capa del servicio, interpolado en la **ruta** de la URL. Infinity interpola `url`, así que es la única forma de cambiar de capa: el número de capa es un segmento de la ruta, no un parámetro.
list.query: Country — H3 R3 : 3,Region — H3 R4 : 4,Province — H3 R5 : 5,Canton — H3 R6 : 6

list.name: capa
list.label: Colour hexagons by
list.description: Infinity no interpola `columns[].selector`, pero sí `computed_columns[].selector`. El target pide los trece conteos con alias fijos y una columna calculada elige uno bajo el nombre estable `n`, que es por el que colorea el `mapConfig` guardado.
list.query: All observations : n_total,Birds : aves,Plants : plantas,Insects : insectos,Reptiles : reptiles,Amphibians : anfibios,Mammals : mamiferos,Fish : peces,Arachnids : aracnidos,Molluscs : moluscos,Fungi : hongos,Protozoa : protozoos,Other : otros

list.name: muestra
list.label: Dots on the map
list.description: El servicio corta en 10 000 rasgos por petición (`maxRecordCountFactor` se satura en 5) y aquí no se pagina, así que esto es el tamaño de la muestra de puntos, no el total. El total lo dice el panel «Esfuerzo».

list.name: desdeAnio
list.label: From year
list.description: Se aplica sobre `observed_on_year`, un entero indexado, en vez de sobre `observed_on`, que es un `TimestampOffset`. Más barato y sin líos de husos horarios. Los hexágonos no lo siguen: son totales históricos.

list.name: taxon
list.label: Taxonomic group
list.description: Sale del propio servicio, así que el mapa nunca puede escribir un valor que no esté en la lista. Es variable de consulta y no textbox porque al limpiar un filtro de kepler `useVariableSync` escribe el literal `$__all`, y con varios valores escribe un array: un textbox no admite ninguno de los dos.
list.definition: taxon_category_name distintos en la capa 0, dentro del ámbito

params.value: latitude BETWEEN -5.1 AND 1.7 AND longitude BETWEEN -92.0 AND -75.0

list.name: area
list.label: Drawn area (WKT)
list.description: La escribe el panel al dibujar un polígono (opción `areaVariable`). El mapa no la lee: si lo hiciera, dibujar encogería su propio conjunto de datos y ya no habría forma de volver a ensancharlo desde el mapa.

list.name: areaRings
list.label: Area (Esri JSON)
list.description: Puente WKT → anillos de Esri. ArcGIS quiere `rings`, el panel publica WKT, y DuckDB es el único conversor del banco. Copiado literal de aqueduct.json.
list.query: SELECT coalesce((SELECT '{"rings":' || json_extract(ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_GeomFromText(wkt)), '$.coordinates')::VARCHAR || ',"spatialReference":{"wkid":4326}}' FROM (SELECT '$area' AS wkt) WHERE length(wkt) > 8), '') AS rings

list.name: lat
list.label: lat
list.description: Destino del enlace «centrar el mapa» de la tabla.

list.name: lng
list.label: lng
list.description: Destino del enlace «centrar el mapa» de la tabla.

options.content:
## Observed biodiversity in Ecuador

**755,403 research-grade observations** uploaded to
[iNaturalist](https://www.inaturalist.org/) by 21,243 people, covering
23,736 species of mainland Ecuador and the Galápagos. They are read live from the
*Feature Service* [iNaturalist Species Observations](https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=996576ae63d4499c924aabea1c3d3768)
in the ArcGIS Living Atlas: **no download and no ETL**, every panel is a query
against the service.

Three things to know so as to read the map properly:

- **The dots are a sample; the hexagons are the total.** The service cuts off at
  10,000 features per request and nothing here pages, so the dot layer is the N
  most recent observations. The H3 cells come already aggregated by the service
  itself and cover all 755,403. The figure to trust is the one in the
  **Observation effort** panel.
- **The hexagons carry no date.** They are historical totals: they follow neither
  "From year" nor the map's time brush. Everything else does.
- **This measures observation effort, not abundance.** iNaturalist records where
  people go and what they photograph. Quito and the Galápagos stand out for their
  observers as much as for their biodiversity.

To narrow things to a particular area, draw it on the map: the side panels and the
tables obey it.

panels.title: Observation effort
panels.description: The authoritative numbers for the extent. ArcGIS computes them without paging, so if they ever stop agreeing with the sum of the hexagons, something is truncating. `count_distinct` is refused on this view, so the two counts come from separate requests.

params.value: latitude BETWEEN -5.1 AND 1.7 AND longitude BETWEEN -92.0 AND -75.0 AND observed_on_year >= $desdeAnio AND taxon_category_name IN (${taxon:sqlstring})
latitude BETWEEN -5.1 AND 1.7 AND longitude BETWEEN -92.0 AND -75.0 AND observed_on_year >= $desdeAnio AND taxon_category_name IN (${taxon:sqlstring})
latitude BETWEEN -5.1 AND 1.7 AND longitude BETWEEN -92.0 AND -75.0 AND observed_on_year >= $desdeAnio AND taxon_category_name IN (${taxon:sqlstring})

panels.title: Where things are observed — H3 hexagons and recent observations
panels.description: Two datasets with deliberately different reach. The **hexagons** are the H3 cells the service itself publishes pre-aggregated: they cover all 755,403 observations of the extent, in one request and without paging. The **dots** are the most recent sample.

params.value: latitude BETWEEN -5.1 AND 1.7 AND longitude BETWEEN -92.0 AND -75.0 AND observed_on_year >= $desdeAnio

panels.title: Taxonomic composition
panels.description: A `groupByFieldsForStatistics` over `taxon_category_name`: a single request for the twelve groups. Grafana opens a context menu when a bar is pressed; the filter is an option in that menu, so it is two clicks, not one.

params.value: latitude BETWEEN -5.1 AND 1.7 AND longitude BETWEEN -92.0 AND -75.0 AND observed_on_year >= $desdeAnio AND taxon_category_name IN (${taxon:sqlstring})

links.title: Filtrar el tablero por este grupo

panels.title: Observations per year
panels.description: Deliberately does **not** follow "From year": this is the panel you look at to decide that value. Its floor is the literal 2016. `anio` is typed as a `string` because a bar chart's X axis needs a string or a time field.

params.value: latitude BETWEEN -5.1 AND 1.7 AND longitude BETWEEN -92.0 AND -75.0 AND observed_on_year >= 2016 AND taxon_category_name IN (${taxon:sqlstring})

panels.title: Seasonality
panels.description: Observations by month of the year, summing the whole history of the extent. It measures **observation effort**, not abundance: it is when people go out to look and to photograph.

params.value: latitude BETWEEN -5.1 AND 1.7 AND longitude BETWEEN -92.0 AND -75.0 AND observed_on_year >= $desdeAnio AND taxon_category_name IN (${taxon:sqlstring})

panels.title: The 20 most observed species
panels.description: `groupByFieldsForStatistics` over the full taxonomic key. The link goes to the taxon's page on iNaturalist, built from the `taxon_id` in that same key: `reference_url` is per observation and does not survive the grouping.

params.value: latitude BETWEEN -5.1 AND 1.7 AND longitude BETWEEN -92.0 AND -75.0 AND observed_on_year >= $desdeAnio AND taxon_category_name IN (${taxon:sqlstring})

panels.title: Recent observations
panels.description: Here `reference_url` does fit, pointing at the specific observation. Two links at two levels: the whole row centres the map, and the "Page" cell opens iNaturalist — an override replaces the default links in that field alone.

params.value: latitude BETWEEN -5.1 AND 1.7 AND longitude BETWEEN -92.0 AND -75.0 AND observed_on_year >= $desdeAnio AND taxon_category_name IN (${taxon:sqlstring})

options.content:
**Source** · [iNaturalist Species Observations](https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=996576ae63d4499c924aabea1c3d3768),
ArcGIS Living Atlas of the World (Esri), a public service needing no credentials.
Original data from [iNaturalist](https://www.inaturalist.org/), a joint initiative
of the California Academy of Sciences and the National Geographic Society;
each observation keeps the licence whoever uploaded it chose.
The service publishes only *research-grade* observations (`quality_grade =
'research'`: dated, georeferenced, with a photo or sound, and of wild organisms)
and runs roughly **a month behind** — the most recent observation in the service
is from 28 July 2026.
**Extent** · a rectangle (`-92.0 −5.1 → −75.0 1.7`), not the country's border:
it drags in strips of Colombia, Peru and ocean. Real clipping is what the polygon
drawn on the map does.
